treeview.comment: Read the exact detected header after common leading trivia; keep the body in the treeview grammar. treeview.md#header-boundary: The [header matcher][keyword] requires common Notation whitespace, `%%` or end of text immediately after the exact keyword.

patterns.comment: Read branchless box rows containing a horizontal bar as decorations; these rows themselves select box mode. A vertical-only row depends on mode selected on other lines, which this line rule cannot determine. treeview.md#line-classification-and-errors: Mode detection and decoration classification are different: a lone vertical bar does not select the mode, whereas a lone horizontal dash can select it and then denote decoration.
patterns.name: comment.block.ignored.mermaid

patterns.comment: Read an authored branch prefix as a structural operator, retaining internal directives. Comment-shaped and metadata-shaped rows keep their ordinary reading. The rule recognizes branch rows without tracking the globally selected box mode. treeview.md#columns-and-prefix-indentation: The prefix consists of all characters through the first branch, then the maximal immediately adjacent run of `─` and `━`, then the following ASCII spaces, with tabs read as four spaces. treeview.md#columns-and-prefix-indentation: After those spaces, another dash is content, not prefix. treeview.md#line-classification-and-errors: Prefix text before the branch is text, not reclassified as earlier-looking keywords or annotations.

Read non-whitespace authored prefix characters as structural operators rather than labels or annotations. treeview.md#line-classification-and-errors: Prefix text before the branch is text, not reclassified as earlier-looking keywords or annotations.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.mermaid

patterns.comment: Reuse shared title and accessibility forms before node content. treeview.md#common-forms: The four common statement forms can read preceding ASCII spaces/tabs. treeview.md#common-forms: An acc-descr-block reads `accDescr`, zero or more common Notation whitespace characters, `{`, any characters through before the first `}`, then that required closer.

Read a class annotation as a separator and a referenced style-class name; keep directives in complete-component gaps. treeview.md#annotations: Each annotation begins with one or more ASCII spaces/tabs. A class-annotation then reads `:::`, zero or more ASCII spaces/tabs, an ASCII letter or underscore, and zero or more ASCII word characters or dashes. The name can be one character. treeview.md#comments-and-boundaries: Allow common trivia between complete authored components, such as keyword and colon, `icon` and `(`, marker and name, or reference and `)`, without supplying missing whitespace.

Reuse native percent comments after a complete class name. treeview.md#comments-and-boundaries: At a native unit start, `%%` reads a shared Comment through before the next LF. Its mark is `%%`; value excludes the mark, and range includes the mark but excludes LF. U+2028/U+2029 and any apparent `}%%` closers stay inside the comment. Hidden newline reads LF separately, including the logical LF at EOF.

Read the icon annotation keyword, argument brackets and complete icon reference; preserve directives between components. treeview.md#annotations: An icon-annotation reads exact lowercase `icon`, `(`, a reference and `)`, without internal whitespace. The reference is zero or more ASCII word characters or dashes, optionally followed by one colon and one or more of those characters. Empty references and `:file` are allowed; a trailing colon, second colon, quoted reference or internal space is not. A following suffix may begin another node.

Read a description annotation modifier followed by unquoted text through line end or a common-comment boundary. treeview.md#annotations: A description-annotation reads `##` and all following characters before CR/LF, possibly none. It includes U+2028/U+2029, percent text and later annotation-looking text on that line. Repeated annotations and any ordering are allowed; a description on a later line is another annotation. A hidden newline or a removed comment line does not detach an annotation from the preceding node.

Reuse the plain double-quoted node label without backslash escapes. treeview.md#names: A quoted-name starts with a single or double quote and closes at the next matching quote under the common and box-drawing rules. Its interior can be empty, cross line feeds, and contain U+2028/U+2029. Backslashes neither protect quotes nor decode escapes. Quotes inside an already-started bare name are ordinary characters.

Reuse the plain single-quoted node label without backslash escapes. treeview.md#names: A quoted-name starts with a single or double quote and closes at the next matching quote under the common and box-drawing rules. Its interior can be empty, cross line feeds, and contain U+2028/U+2029. Backslashes neither protect quotes nor decode escapes. Quotes inside an already-started bare name are ordinary characters.

Read a native percent comment at a unit start, including after a quoted node or icon. treeview.md#comments-and-boundaries: At a native unit start, `%%` reads a shared Comment through before the next LF. Its mark is `%%`; value excludes the mark, and range includes the mark but excludes LF. U+2028/U+2029 and any apparent `}%%` closers stay inside the comment. Hidden newline reads LF separately, including the logical LF at EOF.

Reuse native percent-comment content through the physical line end. treeview.md#comments-and-boundaries: At a native unit start, `%%` reads a shared Comment through before the next LF. Its mark is `%%`; value excludes the mark, and range includes the mark but excludes LF. U+2028/U+2029 and any apparent `}%%` closers stay inside the comment. Hidden newline reads LF separately, including the logical LF at EOF.

Read a bare node as its displayed label, keeping interior quotes and directives in the label and stopping before annotations or common comments. treeview.md#names: A bare-name begins with any character except ASCII space/tab, CR/LF, single quote or double quote, provided `:::`, `icon(` and `##` do not begin there. Read through before CR/LF, but stop before ASCII space/tab followed by one of: `:::` and optional ASCII space/tab and an ASCII letter or underscore; `icon(`; or `##`. The name may otherwise contain whitespace, quotes, percent text, punctuation and Unicode characters.
